newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Harvest in Yugo grain area could end in six days.
newsitem.headline: Harvest in Yugo grain area could end in six days.

text.p: Wheat harvesting in Yugoslavia's major grain area of Vojvodina could be completed in five to six days if weather permits, Tanjug news agency said on Wednesday.

"Due to almost daily rainfall, only 53.6 percent of the total wheat area of 356,306 hectares in Vojvodina has been reaped since the harvest began," the agency quoted Milorad Djilas, vice-president of the regional government, as saying.
"The average yield on the harvested area was 4.18 tonnes per ha with 4.4 tonnes per ha on socially owned and 4.0 tonnes on private farms," he added.

According to first preliminary statistical forecasts, the average yield in Vojvodina would be 3.82 tonnes per ha. Vojvodina has produced some 800,000 tonnes of bread wheat by now, 78 percent of which has already been stored, Djilas said.
Frequent rain slowed harvesting and increased grain moisture, which ranges from 13 to 21 percent. Heavy rains and hailstorms in June and early July damaged 32,000 ha of wheat in Vojvodinay.
After a few sunny days, forecasters announced another wet spell as of July 25 but saw more stable weather and higher temperatures in the first half next week.

Total wheat area in Yugoslavia this year stands at 817,600 ha, up 235,000 ha on the area sown in 1995. The government expected average yields of 3.58 tonnes per hectare, above the first statistical forecast of 3.44 tonnes.
Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce said on Tuesday the wheat crop could fall below forecast because of the adverse effects of rain on already ripe grains.
Yields were falling due to a drop in grain quality and if rains continue it could mean that only wheat for feed rather than bread would be harvested, the Chamber said.

Estimates for the Yugoslav wheat crop range from 2.8 to three million tonnes this year which would satisfy domestic needs and leave 300-500,000 tonnes for exports. --Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
